claims.statement: For every nonconstant Boolean gate at every interior product bias, the common-sign entropic Booleanity projection K_com, defined by minimizing D_2(R||Q_r) over spectral magnitude laws with the same occurrence marginals that admit one common Fourier sign assignment satisfying all biased Boolean multiplication equations simultaneously, satisfies K_occ >= K_com and K_com >= max_{U!=empty} g_U^2/(4 v L_U^2 ln 2).

For F_m(y,x)=y(1-2 1_{x=0}) with p=2^{1-m}, the common-sign feasible spectral magnitude law is unique; hence K_com=K_occ=m h_2(p)-H(P_m). For m>=5, K_com >= (m-1)(m-5)p, while the equation-by-equation max-gap certificate is <= p/ln 2. Therefore K_com/(I(F_m)-1) grows at least linearly whereas the max-gap certificate divided by I(F_m)-1 tends to zero.
claims.verification: Analytic proof; deterministic numerical sanity check in CHECK.py/CHECK_OUTPUT.txt.

claims.statement: In the exact selector notation of fleet02/B13, (1-t)v_0 K_0+t v_1 K_1 is bounded below by the corresponding weighted child common-sign certificates, which in turn dominate the partner paired max-gap bank without introducing the selector condition-number factor.

next_unpaid_implication: Lower-bound K_com by the actual negative first-moment Bellman residual for every gate/bias of a surviving candidate potential, or prove the selector recursion plus child K_com banks necessarily supplies that payment, with at most O(I) loss on sparse suspensions.
